verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.1:2: To Timothy, beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.1:3: I give thanks to God, whom I serve from my forefathers with a clear conscience, as I unceasingly remember you in my supplications night and day,
verses.1:4: earnestly longing to see you, mindful of your tears, so that I may be filled with joy,
verses.1:5: being reminded of the unfeigned faith within you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced that it is in you as well.
verses.1:6: For this cause I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
verses.1:7: For God did not give us a spirit of timidity, but of power and love and self-discipline.
verses.1:8: Therefore do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me His prisoner; rather, share in hardship for the gospel according to the power of God,
verses.1:9: who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
verses.1:10: yet has now been made manifest through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and incorruption to light through the gospel,
verses.1:11: for which I was appointed a herald, and an apostle, and a teacher.
verses.1:12: For this cause I also suffer these things, yet I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard my deposit until that Day.
verses.1:13: Retain the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
verses.1:14: Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
verses.1:15: You know this, that all who are in Asia turned away from me, among whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes.
verses.1:16: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain;
verses.1:17: rather, when he arrived in Rome, he diligently searched for me and found me—
verses.1:18: may the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that Day—and you know very well how many ways he ministered in Ephesus.
verses.2:1: You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus;
verses.2:2: and the things you heard from me before many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be competent to teach others also.
verses.2:3: Share in hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
verses.2:4: No one serving as a soldier becomes entangled in the affairs of daily life, so that he may please the one who enlisted him.
verses.2:5: Moreover, if anyone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
verses.2:6: The hardworking farmer ought to be the first to partake of the fruits.
verses.2:7: Reflect on what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.
verses.2:8: Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the seed of David, according to my gospel,
verses.2:9: for which I suffer hardship even to the point of bonds, like a criminal; yet the word of God is not bound.
verses.2:10: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
verses.2:11: Faithful is the saying: For if we died with Him, we shall also live with Him;
verses.2:12: if we endure, we shall also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us;
verses.2:13: if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
verses.2:14: Remind them of these things, solemnly charging them before God not to dispute about words, which is of no use, to the ruin of those who hear.
verses.2:15: Strive diligently to present yourself approved to God, a workman who has no cause for shame, rightly expounding the word of truth.
verses.2:16: But avoid profane, empty chatter, for they will advance further into ungodliness,
verses.2:17: and their talk will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
verses.2:18: who have swerved from the truth, claiming that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are overturning the faith of some.
verses.2:19: Yet the firm foundation of God stands fast, bearing this seal: "The Lord knows those who are His," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity."
verses.2:20: Now in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earthenware, some for honor and others for dishonor.
verses.2:21: Therefore, if anyone purifies himself from these, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, made ready for every good work.
verses.2:22: Now flee youthful passions, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart.
verses.2:23: And refuse foolish and uninstructed disputes, knowing that they breed quarrels.
verses.2:24: For a servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, apt to teach, forbearing,
verses.2:25: in meekness instructing those who oppose, so that perhaps God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth,
verses.2:26: and that they may return to soberness out of the devil's snare, having been captured by him to do his will.
verses.3:1: But understand this, that in the last days grievous times will set in:
verses.3:2: for men will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, revilers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
verses.3:3: without natural affection, irreconcilable, slanderers, unrestrained, fierce, haters of what is good,
verses.3:4: treacherous, reckless, swollen with conceit, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
verses.3:5: holding an outward form of godliness, yet having denied its power. Turn away from such as these.
verses.3:6: For among them are those who creep into households and take captive weak women weighed down with sins, swayed by various passions,
verses.3:7: ever learning, yet never able to attain to the knowledge of the truth.
verses.3:8: And just as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so these also withstand the truth—men corrupted in mind, disqualified regarding the faith.
verses.3:9: Yet they will advance no further, for their folly will be evident to all, just as theirs also became.
verses.3:10: You, however, have closely followed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my longsuffering, my love, my steadfastness,
verses.3:11: my persecutions and sufferings—such as befell me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra—what persecutions I endured! Yet out of them all the Lord delivered me.
verses.3:12: Indeed, all who desire to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted;
verses.3:13: whereas wicked men and impostors will advance from bad to worse, leading others astray and being led astray themselves.
verses.3:14: You, however, abide in the things you have learned and of which you have become convinced, knowing from whom you learned them,
verses.3:15: and that from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
verses.3:16: All Scripture is God-breathed and beneficial for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for discipline in righteousness,
verses.3:17: so that the man of God may be competent, thoroughly furnished for every good work.
verses.4:1: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is about to judge the living and the dead, and by His appearing and His kingdom:
verses.4:2: Preach the word; stand ready in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and exhort with all longsuffering and instruction.
verses.4:3: For a time shall come when they will not bear with sound doctrine, but according to their own desires they will heap up teachers for themselves, having itching ears,
verses.4:4: and they shall turn away their hearing from the truth, and be turned aside to fables.
verses.4:5: But you, remain sober-minded in all things, endure affliction, perform the work of an evangelist, fully accomplish your ministry.
verses.4:6: For I am even now being poured out as a drink offering, and the season of my departure has arrived.
verses.4:7: I have fought the noble fight, I have completed the course, I have preserved the faith.
verses.4:8: Now there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall award to me on that day—and not to me alone, but also to all who have loved His appearing.
verses.4:9: Strive to come to me quickly;
verses.4:10: for Demas forsook me, having loved this present age, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
verses.4:11: Luke alone is with me. Take Mark along and bring him with you, for he is helpful to me in ministry.
verses.4:12: As for Tychicus, I sent him to Ephesus.
verses.4:13: When you come, bring the cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, and the scrolls, above all the parchments.
verses.4:14: Alexander the coppersmith inflicted much harm upon me—the Lord shall repay him according to his works.
verses.4:15: You also must guard yourself against him, for he fiercely opposed our words.
verses.4:16: At my first defense no one came to my side, but all forsook me—may it not be reckoned against them.
verses.4:17: Yet the Lord stood at my side and gave me strength, so that through me the proclamation might be brought to fullness and all the Gentiles might hear; and I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
verses.4:18: The Lord shall deliver me from every wicked deed and preserve me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:19: Greet Prisca and Aquila, as well as the household of Onesiphorus.
verses.4:20: Erastus stayed at Corinth, and Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.
verses.4:21: Strive to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brethren send you greetings.
verses.4:22: May the Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.

notes.1:7: The Greek term rendered "timidity" (deilia) denotes cowardice or faintheartedness, while "self-discipline" (sophronismos) conveys sober-mindedness and self-control.
notes.1:11: The critical Greek text reads "a herald, and an apostle, and a teacher," without the phrase "of the Gentiles" found in later manuscripts.
notes.1:12: "My deposit" (ten paratheken mou) may refer either to what Paul has entrusted to God for safekeeping or to the gospel ministry God has entrusted to Paul (compare 1:14).
notes.1:18: The solemn repetition "the Lord ... from the Lord" reflects the Greek text (ho kyrios ... para kyriou), emphasizing the mercy granted on the final Day of judgment.
notes.2:7: The critical Greek text uses the future indicative "will give" (dosei) rather than the optative wish "may give."
notes.2:15: "Rightly expounding" translates orthotomounta, literally "cutting straight," a metaphor for faithfully and accurately presenting the message of truth.
notes.2:19: The critical Greek text reads "the name of the Lord" (kyriou), echoing Old Testament wording (compare Numbers 16:5, 26; Isaiah 26:13), rather than "the name of Christ."
notes.2:26: The two Greek pronouns ("by him" and "his") are syntactically debated: both may refer to the devil, or the first may refer to the devil (or the Lord's servant) and the second to God ("to do His will").
notes.3:8: Jannes and Jambres are the names preserved in Jewish tradition for the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses (Exodus 7:11, 22).
notes.3:14: The Greek pronoun "whom" (tinon) is plural in the critical text, encompassing not only Paul but also Timothy's mother Eunice and grandmother Lois (compare 1:5; 3:15).
notes.3:16: "God-breathed" translates theopneustos; while the clause may also be read "Every God-breathed Scripture is also beneficial," the predicate construction "All Scripture is God-breathed and beneficial" is the standard reading.
notes.4:1: The critical Greek text reads "Christ Jesus" and introduces "His appearing and His kingdom" with "and" as part of the solemn adjuration, whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "the Lord Jesus Christ" and "at His appearing."
notes.4:6: The verb rendered "being poured out as a drink offering" recalls the sacrificial libation (cf. Philippians 2:17), while the Greek noun for "departure" (analysis) was commonly used for unmooring a ship or striking camp.
notes.4:14: The Greek text here uses the future indicative "shall repay" as a confident statement echoing Psalm 62:12 (LXX 61:13), whereas later manuscripts read the optative wish "may the Lord repay."
notes.4:22: The critical text reads simply "the Lord" without "Jesus Christ" and ends without "Amen." Notably, the pronoun shifts from singular "your spirit" (addressed to Timothy) to plural "you all" (extending the blessing to the congregation).
